T1 – Apple Tree (Malus species) – Crown Reduction Location: Within the garden of 64 Bath Road, immediately adjacent to the boundary with 62 Bath Road. Proposed works: Reduce the entire crown evenly back to the established previous pruning points (knuckles), as agreed in onsite visit today 08/10/26 retaining the main trunk and established framework to allow future regrowth. Reason: Several overhead telephone and broadband cables pass through the canopy. Pruning only the branches interfering with these cables would leave the crown significantly unbalanced, particularly as the tree already leans towards the property. The trunk is also hollow, raising concerns regarding structural stability. Reducing the crown evenly to its previous pruning points will reduce the canopy weight, avoid creating an uneven load and minimise interference with the overhead cables while retaining the tree. T2 – Conifer – Complete Removal Location: Along the retaining wall forming the boundary between 64 and 66 Bath Road. Proposed works: Fell and remove the conifer to ground level. Reason: The tree is situated immediately adjacent to the existing retaining wall, which requires essential structural repairs. Its position and associated root system obstruct the necessary repair works. T3 – Conifer – Complete Removal Location: Along the same retaining wall between 64 and 66 Bath Road, adjacent to T2. Proposed works: Fell and remove the conifer. Reason: As with T2, the tree’s proximity to the retaining wall obstructs essential structural repairs. Removal is required to facilitate these works safely and effectively. Additional Information All three trees and the proposed works were discussed with the Worcester City Council Tree Officer during a site visit on 8 October 2026. The locations of T1, T2 and T3 are identified on the accompanying Tree Works Plan, with supporting photographs showing the trees and proposed pruning locations. Replacement Planting No replacement trees are proposed at this stage because the removal of T2 and T3 is necessary to facilitate repairs to the existing retaining wall. The apple tree (T1) will be retained and allowed to regenerate.

proposal: The proposed works relate to a mature silver birch tree situated within the rear garden of the property, in close proximity to the adjoining residential property and its garden. A previous application for tree works consent (Ref: 21/00555/CAN) was submitted for similar works; however, these were not subsequently undertaken. Since the submission of the original application, the tree has continued to grow, resulting in an increased crown spread and a greater impact on the neighbouring property. Consequently, a more substantial reduction is now proposed to address the current concerns. The proposed works comprise a crown reduction of approximately 4–5 metres, together with a crown lift of approximately 2–3 metres. The intention is to reduce the overall size and lateral spread of the crown, improve natural light to the neighbouring property and minimise the risk of further damage to the adjacent garage roof. The proposed works are intended to provide a proportionate and considered management solution, addressing the impact of the tree on the neighbouring property whilst retaining the tree within the landscape and maintaining its long-term health and structural integrity. All works will be undertaken in accordance with BS 3998:2010 – Tree Work Recommendations, with appropriate consideration given to the natural growth characteristics and physiological requirements of the species.
